title: Print a slice's orchestrator brief with ai relay-brief
lead: `slicer ai relay-brief ID --worktree PATH --branch NAME --run RUN --step N` prints the slice-specific orchestrator brief, filled from the item, the role matrix, the finish step and a project template, so the outer session stops assembling briefs by hand.
findings_note: outer-session wishlist 2026-10-16, item 1: hand-assembled briefs caused wrong commit titles and parallel names
boundary: **Not in this slice:** spawning agents; recording the run (the outer session still runs `relay-run begin`/`step`); briefs for implementer, reviewer and gate roles (the orchestrator writes those); this repo's own environment lines, which the owner sets with `template set` after it lands.

sections.heading: Why
Files
Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_AiRelayBrief_FillsIdTitleRunStepAndCommitTitle`
- `test_AiRelayBrief_RolesComeFromRecommend`: a matrix row change shows in the brief.
- `test_AiRelayBrief_HandoffProject_HasFinishOverride` and `test_AiRelayBrief_DoneProject_NoOverride`
- `test_AiRelayBrief_Parallel_NamesTheOtherSlice`: `--parallel s2` names s2 and not the item itself.
- `test_AiRelayBrief_ProjectTemplate_Used`: after `template set relay-brief.md`, the custom ENVIRONMENT text appears.
- `test_AiRelayBrief_NoSlice_Unspecified`

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Add the template and `relay_brief`, then the CLI.
3. Generate the s308 brief from this session's inputs and diff it against the hand-built one, which is saved in the outer scratchpad; paste the differences into the note.
4. Docs and CHANGELOG; mutation-check (drop `--parallel`; ignore the template override).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
